title: Dualization of hard samples is an involution
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$, and let $\omega$ be any hard sample: a distinguished coordinate $T \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, two bits recording Alice's and Bob's values there, and an assignment of a disjoint coordinate (neither, left-only, or right-only) to every coordinate. Applying the dualization map to $\omega$ twice returns $\omega$ itself; that is, the dualization — which reverses the coordinate order, interchanges Alice's and Bob's bits at the distinguished coordinate, and swaps the two sides of every coordinate assignment — is an involution.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
ω is an arbitrary hard sample
replaced: Dualizing a hard sample twice recovers the original sample.
